prompt: For each new invoice PDF in the inbox folder, read the total; if it's over 10,000 forward it for finance director approval by email, otherwise send it to the department manager, then move the file to the pending approval folder.

Check the unread AP emails whose subject mentions bank details or change of account; for each one ask AI whether it's really a request to change vendor bank details, and if yes forward it to the vendor master team with a fraud-check warning and flag it.

Download the bank's payment status report from SFTP, read it, keep the rows with status RJCT, and for each rejected payment set its status to rejected in the payments database; then email AP the list of rejected payments.

For each payment status callback file in the inbox folder, compute the HMAC signature of its content with our webhook secret, compare it with the signature in the matching .sig file, and move the callback to verified if they match or to quarantine if not.

For each unread email in the Bug Reports folder that has screenshots, save the PNG attachments, have the AI describe the error shown, create a ServiceNow incident with that description and attach the screenshots to it.

Read today's messages in the #customer-feedback Slack channel and, for every message that mentions a bug, crash or error, open a Zendesk ticket with the message text and reply in the Slack thread with the ticket link.

Check the delivery notes folder for PDFs that came in during the last day; if there are any, print them on the warehouse printer and move them to the printed folder, otherwise just log that there was nothing to print.

Take the big scanned batch PDF, split it into separate documents at the blank separator pages, then OCR each piece, pull out the invoice number after 'Invoice No' and rename the file to that number. If a piece can't be read, log it and move on.

Read the test points of our regression suite in Azure DevOps, keep the ones whose outcome is Failed, and for each create a Bug work item; then email QA lead how many failed, or that everything passed.
List all repositories of our GitHub organization, save them as a CSV file and upload that file to the platform team's Slack channel.

Check the consolidation mailbox for unread emails from the subsidiaries, save their trial balance CSV attachments to the TB folder, and load each file into the staging trial balance table in our consolidation database, logging any file that fails to load.
Check on the revenue mart rebuild statement in Snowflake; if it's still running past its window, cancel it and email the BI team with the status message, otherwise log how it finished.

Sign in to the recruiting mailbox, go through unread emails with 'Background verification' in the subject, save their PDF attachments into the BGV folder, mark each email read, and at the end email the HR ops team how many came in.

In the training tracker Excel, find new joiners whose mandatory training status isn't Completed and email each one a reminder; then post in the HR Teams channel how many were reminded. If everyone is done, log it.
Every evening find all running EC2 instances tagged as dev or test, stop them, wait until they're actually stopped and email the cloud team how many were shut down.
Sign in to ServiceNow with our OAuth client, get all open incidents assigned to the Network group, ping the host named on each one and add the result as a work note, then revoke the token.
Open the price schedule workbook, delete the Internal Margins sheet, lock the Prices sheet with a password, save it as a separate supplier copy and email that copy to the supplier.
On a DocuSign envelope, go through the recipients and find the one with the wrong email address; change it to the correct address and resend to them.

Read the project phases from our planning Google Sheet, where each row has a phase name and how many working days after kickoff it ends. For each phase work out the end date from the kickoff date, skipping holidays, and add an all-day milestone to the project Outlook calendar with the team invited.

Find a free one-hour slot in the next 7 days when the whole project team is available in Outlook and book the sprint review meeting in the first slot found. If no slot works, email me so I can sort it out manually.
In the quotes Google Sheet, mark every quote whose valid-until date has passed and is not already accepted as Expired in the status column, then write the sheet back.
Read our quote tracker Google Sheet, keep only quotes with status Sent, and for each one sent more than 7 days ago email the customer contact a polite follow-up from Gmail.
Pull the product catalogue from the shop's API, take the items list, and build a new Excel workbook with them, with a bold header row and fitted columns.
Open the regulator's publications page, collect all the document links, and for each link that points to a PDF download it into our regulations folder.
